title: Quantum Sphaera Companion: A Structure-First Mathematical Unfolding — full Companion and physics paper
description:
Quantum Sphaera Companion v5.6.0 is a minor version of the database-backed v5 release. As before, it comprises two complementary English documents from one source snapshot: the full Companion with its research history, and the physics paper Graded carriers and physical readouts: conditions for mass and geometric interpretation.

New in the full Companion are the research layers v4.10.0-r69 to r75. They record: a naming convention for the frames (rest frame R, matter frame M, dual frame T, formerly tachyon frame, light point P) and for the two lepton sectors (Re and Im sector, a reading under H99), decided by the author on 26 November 2026 (r69); port weights against amplitudes and the position of the frames on the state sphere of the compensator, with a correction to r69.4 that changes no verdict (r70); a Friedman coincidence scan as a diagnostic tool (r71); a restatement of the photon-clock guard (r72); that the common offset of the Brannen phases of both lepton sectors is a dimensionless rotation angle phi and not a scale, that the branch of the data is chosen without a scale by the sign of a cubic spectral invariant, a sign set by the author, that the value phi = 0.0395773 is not derived by any route tried and remains the one measured number of the lepton picture, and a balance in which three numbers carry all six lepton masses (tests H213 to H227, r73); further attempts to derive phi (asymptote and flow, a loosening of the frame exchange at order six, the symmetry point in the matter frame, cosmic expansion as a clock, a backward search for a breaker of the sector exchange, locking to eight positions, a common fine step, a Casimir twist), all refuted or without a hit, an exploration of an inner and an outer field with a Casimir gap, and the clarification of a double counting in which phi carries the offset and the cubic coefficient only its sign, with no verdict changed; on the author's decision of 28 November 2026 the value of phi is left open and the strand rests (H228 to H236, r74); and a dated register of the model state and its predictions for this version as of 28 November 2026 (r75).

Predictions of this version (register r75, as of 28 November 2026): normal neutrino mass ordering; sum of neutrino masses 59.30 ± 0.24 meV; m1, m2, m3 = 0.379, 8.81, 50.11 meV; effective beta-decay mass 8.87 meV; effective double-beta mass 1.3 to 4.0 meV; the ratio of the mass splittings R = 0.030839; three mutually exclusive readings of sin^2 theta12 and a theta12–CP correlation that JUNO and DUNE can test; theta23, theta13 and delta_CP; Omega_m = beta_sym^2 = 0.30185; m_W = 80.3615 GeV; m_tau. For each entry the register states what is derived, what is set and what is measured: phi = 0.0395773 is a measured input; the branch sign is a setting; beta_sym = 0.5494056410 is computed from the counting rule adopted as a postulate on 26 November 2026, not derived; K = 2/3 rests on the postulate of equal standing of the frames; the Brannen form is set; the scales of the two sectors are fitted. Entries found after the data are marked as such. Version rule of the author: every public version records its model state with its predictions; corrections appear only in a later version with a stated reason (model progress or error), never as a readjustment after a new measurement; a test counts against the version fixed before the measurement. Earlier versions remain visible.

New in the physics paper: a development subsection on the lepton phase in the masses part (r69 to r74) and a dated section with the predictions of this version in the limits part (r75). The research catalogue gains eight entries.

Scope: this is a conditional mathematical-physics research programme, not a completed unified theory. No native lepton spectrum, absolute physical mass scale, general gravitational field equations or closure of the open problems is established by this release. The counting rule and the equal standing of the frames are postulates, not derived. OP1 to OP5, C5 and C6/T2 remain open; no guard is closed. No prediction has been decided by data. Database registration, hashes and provenance checks do not constitute proof of physical interpretation. The manuscript has undergone documented self-review, not independent peer review.

The package contains two English PDFs, compilable sources, a database snapshot and checksum manifests. Both document editions retain open argument-review obligations.

Companion articles built on this version: the German preprint 0.5.0 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.24632440) and the stand-alone English physics article "One Object, Three Frames" 1.2.0 (in preparation). Version DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24632437. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19210728.
notes: Two complementary English documents in one versioned Companion record. The version DOI identifies the whole package. The German reader edition is excluded. Scientific guards and incomplete argument-review flags remain unchanged. Reservation and upload do not constitute publication.
